summary: Every role tier now pins a model and an effort, the owner's choice of 1 Oct 2026 on #349, so no role follows the session's effort level, which some sessions run at `max`, and no role defaults to `max` or `ultra`. The package has three role tiers, `high`, `medium` and `low`, beside the `inherit` profile: the `lens` and `mechanical` tiers that came with the review panel and mechanical pass variants are gone, and all eight generated variants, the four `-lens` readers and the four `-mechanical` writers, run on the `low` tier, where the values chosen for them stay. Against v0.6.0: on Claude Code, where no tier set an effort, the high tier moves from the `opus` alias to `claude-opus-5-5` at `xhigh`, the medium tier (the developers, DevOps, QA, the Delivery Coordinator, the Product Owner and the UX designer) moves from the `sonnet` alias to `claude-opus-5-5` at `medium`, and the low tier, which no role ran, moves from the `haiku` alias to `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `high` and now runs every variant; on Codex, where roles named no model, every tier runs `gpt-6.1-sol` at `xhigh`: the high tier moves from effort `high`, the medium tier from `medium` and the low tier from `low`. Each host's `model-catalog.json` is keyed by exact model ID and each tier of its `execution-profiles.json` names its model directly, so the model class layer (`frontier`, `strong` and `fast`) is gone; a model bump renames the catalog entry and every tier on it. The catalogs keep `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and `gpt-6-luna`, which no tier runs. On a subscription plan every Claude Code role outside the low tier therefore draws on the Opus usage limit. This supersedes what `pinned-role-models` says of the model classes, of the efforts, of the Claude medium tier and of the Codex tiers, what `mechanical-pass-tier` says of the `mechanical` tier and the classes its variants run, and what `review-panel-lens-variants` says of the `lens` tier. The model and effort lines of rendered agents stay the named exception to default equivalence, and `docs/authoring.md` gives the reasons with their sources. A role whose pinned model cannot run now falls back to the session's model with a visible warning. On Claude Code an organization model policy already substitutes the session's model with Claude Code's own warning; for a model that Claude Code's wording names as not found, refused or too new for the installed Claude Code, the host contract has the coordinator tell the user and, only when the failed run changed nothing (its task is read-only, or the `task_inputs.py` invocation that derived its manifest still passes with `--expected-hash`, which compares the content `git status` would not show, such as a further edit to an already modified file), spawn the same role once more with `model` set to the session's family alias, stopping if that spawn fails too, and a new plugin hook on `Agent` (`model_fallback.py` under `PostToolUseFailure` and `PostToolUse`) adds the warning and that instruction to a foreground failure and warns when a role started on another model than its pin; it matches only Claude Code's model wording (error type `model_not_found`, `There's an issue with the selected model`, `is not available on your ... deployment` and the plan and access forms), since a subagent's error detail names the pin for any API error. The hook stays silent for a spawn that passes `model` and under `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE`, so a model the user chose never triggers it and the re-spawn never repeats; `tools/validate.py` requires it in the Claude hooks. On Codex no runtime setting moves a role off its pinned model, so setup and refresh judge each pinned model against Codex's own model list, as `host-model-listing` describes, and `generate_codex_project.py apply --inherit-model <model>` renders the roles of one model without `model`, keeping `model_reasoning_effort`, and records that until `--restore-model <model>` or `--execution-profile auto`. The Codex host contract has the coordinator run it and start the same role again when a spawn ends in `Agent errored: ...` that names its pinned model as unknown, unsupported, not found or not supported with the account and the failed run changed nothing, never for a rate limit or another error; when that start errors too, `--restore-model <model>` renders the pin again before the coordinator stops, so no fallback stays recorded that no successful start backs. `--execution-profile auto` restores every pin and judges them again. `--execution-profile inherit` now keeps each role's `model_reasoning_effort`, so an inherited role no longer runs the parent's effort, `low` by default for Sol in Codex 0.159.
